description: Pins protocol::encode_new_note_blob_raw + protocol::decode_note byte mapping for the MY01 per-note blob format across realistic plaintext sizes (10 B / 1 KB / 100 KB) and the non-distinguishing AEAD-stage rejection surface. content_type is HARDCODED to 'text/markdown' in aad_note_content_encrypt — no v0.1 parameter to vary. Cases generated by `cargo test -p protocol --lib emit_myn_blob_vectors_for_paste -- --ignored` (in protocol/src/blob.rs). The 100-KB plaintext case is inlined as a ~200-KB hex string; cases.json total ≈ 250 KB — git-friendly, `jq`-readable.

cases.description: Encode a 10-byte plaintext `Hello,Myne` (ASCII). Smallest representative case — exercises the encoder's framing without significant ciphertext volume. Expected blob length = 76 (header_prefix + content_nonce + ciphertext_len) + 10 (plaintext) + 32 (CTX tag) = 118 bytes.
Encode a 1024-byte plaintext where byte i = (i mod 256). Mid-size case — proves the encoder handles a full XChaCha20 keystream block plus tail. Expected blob length = 76 + 1024 + 32 = 1132 bytes.

Encode a 102400-byte plaintext where byte i = (i mod 256). Near-realistic note size; proves the encoder remains correct at scale without the MAX_PLAINTEXT_LEN cap firing (cap is 16 MiB). Expected blob length = 76 + 102400 + 32 = 102508 bytes. The inlined hex string is ~205 KB — the largest single field in any landed cases.json.

Round-trip the 1-KB blob from case 2 back to the same plaintext under the matching items_key + items_key_id + note_uuid. Proves the decoder's structural parse + outer-AEAD unwrap of item_key + inner-AEAD decrypt of ciphertext all reconstruct the canonical plaintext bytes.

Take the 10-byte blob from case 1 and flip one byte at OFFSET_CIPHERTEXT (the first byte of the encrypted content region) via XOR 0xFF. Decoder MUST surface DecryptError::CannotDecrypt — the CTX commitment construction (SHA-256 over key||nonce||AAD-len||AAD||Poly1305-tag) catches the modification: the recomputed Poly1305 tag changes, the recomputed CTX commitment changes, the constant-time comparison fails. Ports MUST NOT distinguish 'tampered ciphertext' from 'wrong key' or 'wrong AAD'; all collapse to the single non-distinguishing variant per spec §6.4.
cases.informational_tamper_description: byte 140 (OFFSET_CIPHERTEXT, first byte of encrypted content) flipped via XOR 0xFF
